answer: An agent economy can make influence depend on a scarce, stake-backed credential rather than on account count. At each epoch, a public beacon supplies unpredictable randomness; agents commit stake before dawn, then a trellis-style random assignment selects a small set of credential holders to validate claims. Splitting into many identities does not create more selection weight, because weight follows the same bonded stake, while each extra credential adds setup and lockup costs. A Sybil attacker must therefore acquire and risk real capital, not merely mint accounts.
